method_card.title: Factors, Multiples & Primes
steps: Break each number into prime factors using a factor tree.
Write it in index form, e.g. \(2^3\times 3\times 5\).
HCF: multiply the shared primes at their lowest powers.
LCM: multiply all primes at their highest powers.
method_card.content:
Factors divide a number exactly; multiples are its times table. A prime has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, so 1 is not prime and 2 is the only even prime.

The HCF is the largest factor two numbers share; the LCM is the smallest multiple they share.

The efficient method is prime factor decomposition: break each number into primes in index form. For the HCF multiply the shared primes at their lowest powers; for the LCM multiply all primes at their highest powers.
method_card.example:
Find the HCF and LCM of 24 and 36

Step 1: \(24 = 2^3 \times 3\) and \(36 = 2^2 \times 3^2\)

Step 2, HCF: shared primes, lowest powers: \(2^2 \times 3 = 12\)

Step 3, LCM: all primes, highest powers: \(2^3 \times 3^2 = 72\)

Answer: HCF = 12, LCM = 72

problem_bank.bronze_description: Find factors, multiples and simple HCFs and LCMs, and test small numbers for being prime.
problem_bank.silver_description: Use prime factorisation to find the HCF and LCM of larger numbers, including worded LCM problems.
problem_bank.gold_description: Solve multi-number LCMs, prime-factorise big numbers, and use HCF × LCM = product in reverse.

bronze.title: Bronze: factors, multiples and primes by hand
steps: Factors divide a number exactly; find them in pairs (1×12, 2×6, 3×4). Multiples are its times table.
A prime has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. Test small numbers by dividing by 2, 3, 5 and 7.
The HCF is the largest factor two numbers share; the LCM is the first multiple they share.

silver.title: Silver: prime factors for HCF and LCM
steps: Break each number into prime factors in index form, e.g. 48 = \(2^4\times 3\).
HCF: multiply the shared primes at their lowest powers.
LCM: multiply all primes at their highest powers. A worded 'next time together' question is an LCM.

gold.title: Gold: multi-number and reverse problems
steps: For three numbers, list every prime that appears, then take each at its highest power (LCM) or lowest shared power (HCF).
Given the HCF and LCM, use HCF × LCM = the product of the two numbers to find a missing one.
For a big number, divide by each prime repeatedly and count the powers.
